messages:
incident-bot: ALERT: P3 -> P1 spike: continuous-batcher queue depth > 75% for us-west-1-runtime-pool. Autoscale failed to respond. Traces: https://ops/redwood/incidents/1859994321 :rotating_light:

sre-bot: runtime/container-monitor reported repeated OOMs and panics on nodes rwp-rt-23, rwp-rt-24. CUDA errors in logs. Investigating.

Maria L.: I'm on it. jumping to the runtime room. anyone seen a config change in the last 30m?

Devin K.: Not from me. last deploy was a model rollout 1h ago but only to canary. @sre-bot can you dump recent deploys?

sre-bot: deploy history for us-west-1 runtime: 
- 1859990720 model-rollout v2.3 -> canary (5% traffic)
- 1859987120 infra: node pool autoscaler bump to 6 -> 6 (no-op)

Hao T.: grabbing logs from rwp-rt-23:
```
[2026-02-27T09:12:54Z] ERROR: cudaMalloc failed: out of memory
[2026-02-27T09:12:54Z] WARN: batcher queue growing: queued_tokens=1.2M, active_batches=0
[2026-02-27T09:12:55Z] ERROR: runtime: container restart due to OOM
[2026-02-27T09:12:58Z] INFO: paging eviction triggered for kv-cache (pageouts=560)
```

Avery R.: Queue shows huge prefix reuse for a single customer (acct-3789). Could be a pathological workload keeping KV cache pinned and preventing normal batching.

Maria L.: Customer impact? any 5xx spikes?

Devin K.: Yes, API error-rate up for a subset of keys. Graphs: https://telemetry/redwood/err/1859994321 -> 500s up 4x for requests hitting us-west-1, latency tail exploding to >10s.

charlie.s: I've flagged affected tenant acct-3789 to support. Sending advisory: "we're investigating elevated latency and errors for your queries in US-WEST".

Maria L.: Immediate mitigation plan: 1) Isolate offending tenant with temporary traffic rule -> route acct-3789 to fallback pool (smaller model, dedicated smaller batches). 2) Drain problematic nodes, force restart batcher process. 3) Apply emergency queue limits: max_queue_tokens=200k, max_queue_time_ms=1200. 4) Notify SRE if node count still under pressure.

Hao T.: I can do (2) and (3) now. Applying queue limits via runtime config:
```
kubectl -n runtime patch configmap continuous-batcher --type merge -p '{"data":{"max_queue_tokens":"200000","max_queue_time_ms":"1200"}}'
# rollout restart batcher
kubectl -n runtime rollout restart deployment/continuous-batcher
```

sre-bot: Applying patch to configmap continuous-batcher... SUCCESS. Rolling restart started.

Devin K.: I'll create the routing rule to divert acct-3789:
```
rwctl routes add --tenant acct-3789 --pool us-west-fallback --model redwood-small-v1 --priority emergency
```

sre-bot: Route added. Traffic for acct-3789 now 100% -> us-west-fallback.

Maria L.: Good. Once nodes drain we should see queue depth drop. @Hao T. any signs of continuous-batcher deadlock or starvation after restart?

Hao T.: After restart we're seeing improved queue drain on rwp-rt-24, but rwp-rt-23 hit kernel OOM and is flapping. Paging activity still elevated, KV cache eviction rate dropping now.

Devin K.: Throttling heavy tenants seemed to immediately reduce tail latency on the dashboard to ~700ms. Still some 500s during container restarts.

Avery R.: Can we temporarily enable per-tenant token caps to avoid recurrence? I can push policy to rate-limit acct-3789 to 30rps.

Maria L.: Yes do that. Also escalate to eng-runtime for a postmortem: possible causes: KV cache growth without backpressure, batching logic allowing unlimited queue growth when eviction/paging occurs, and autoscaler not reacting due to resource fragmentation.

charlie.s: Support updated customer with ETA ~30m and offered temporary throttling. They accepted.

Devin K.: Noting next steps: - collect heap/KV stats from crashed nodes - add instrumentation for batch queue length per-tenant - add circuit breaker in batcher when queued_tokens > threshold -> reject/route to fallback - run load test to reproduce prefix-pinned workload. I'll open an incident ticket and assign to eng-runtime.

Maria L.: Thanks. Assigning severity P1 due to multi-node impact and customer errors. @eng-runtime please join: @Hao T., @Devin K., @Avery R.

incident-bot: INCIDENT CREATED: 1859994321 | P1 | continuous-batcher queue runaway -> multi-node OOMs. Incident channel: #inc-1859994321. Pager rotation: on-call eng-runtime.

Hao T.: quick note: during restart I captured one more stack where batcher goroutine showed blocked on queue manager: "waiting on condition variable, queue_size > 0 but no batch creation thread running" — suggests a deadlock path when page eviction occurs. Saving core dump and attaching to ticket.

Maria L.: Great work everyone. I'll stay on the incident until nodes stabilize and the routing rule proves effective. Devin please own the postmortem and mitigation RFC for a permanent fix.

Devin K.: Will do. Opening incident ticket with initial summary and action items.

Avery R.: +1. lets also add an alert for "queue growth without batch throughput" to catch this earlier.

charlie.s: Support will follow up with the customer when we have resolution.

sre-bot: Health check: queue depth dropping to 18%, error-rate trending down to baseline. Node rwp-rt-23 remains in CrashLoopBackOff (OOM) and is cordoned for deeper investigation.

Maria L.: Handing off to on-call evening shift @Avery R. I'll leave notes in the incident channel. If anything regresses ping me. :white_check_mark:

Avery R.: Taking handoff. I'll monitor the fallback pool and work with infra to repro. Thanks all.

incident-bot: INCIDENT UPDATED: mitigation in progress, P1 -> under control, notifications sent to affected tenants.
